 CORAM : SHIVKUMAR DIGE, J.

ORAL JUDGMENT :-
.
This appeal is preferred by the Appellant-Claimant for enhancement of compensation.
2. It is contention of learned counsel for the Appellant- Claimant that, due to accidental injuries, the Claimant has lost vision of left eye.
He has suffered 20% permanent physical disability, but the Tribunal has awarded lump-sump compensation of Rs.1,30,000/-, which is erroneous.
The learned counsel further submitted that, the Claimant was working as cleaner and labourer and earning Rs.4,000/- per month as salary.
The Tribunal has not applied multiplier.
No future prospects is awarded.
Due to permanent physical disability the Claimant has lost his job.
Hence, requested to allow the Appeal.
3. It is contention of learned counsel for the Respondent-Insurance Company that, the Tribunal has passed well reasoned order.
No evidence is produced on record to prove N.S. Kamble page 2 of 8 90-FA-409-2008-JUDG.doc the income and disability of the Claimant and requested to dismiss the Appeal.
4. I have heard both learned counsel.
Perused judgment and order passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal ('The Tribunal' for short), Kolhpaur.
5. It is Claimant's case that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered fractures and he has lost the vision of left eye.
To prove this fact PW-2 Doctor Ajit Shinde has been examined by the Claimant.
He has stated that, after the accident the Claimant was admitted in his hospital on 8 th April 2005 and he was operated.
There was fracture on left ankle of the Claimant.
He operated the Claimant, and screw was fixed in his ankle.
He has further stated that, CT Scan showed that, there was nasal bone fracture, collection in sinuse and bulging of left eye ball.
The said injury was treated by another doctor.
The Claimant was coming to me for follow-up for about next four months after discharge.

sentences.text: He was admitted for 5 days and he has paid the charges for it.

Later on Claimant N.S.
Kamble page 3 of 8 90-FA-409-2008-JUDG.doc had come to meet him for the assessment of disability and he evaluated him radiologically and clinically, and issued disability certificate showing permanent physical disability as there was restriction of the movement of 20% to left ankle.
In cross- examination he has admitted that, the Claimant can do job of a cleaner.
The Disability Certificate has not been issued as per format of Motor Vehicle Act.

6. To prove the disability of eye the Claimant has examined PW-3 Doctor Abhijit Tagare, he has stated that he conducted eye examination of the Claimant, he found that his right eye was not normal as regards left eye, externally it was normal but his vision was only 6/24, not improving with glasses from fundus (retina and optic nerve) examination there was pallor of the disc.
It was suggestive of traumatic optic neuropathy.
On visual field analysis his right eye vision on field was normal but the left eye visual field showed depression of vision in upper and lower halves.
There is no active treatment for this disorder.
He explained him about it.
Now the same condition persists with his eyes.
Therefore, it can be said that he N.S. Kamble page 4 of 8 90-FA-409-2008-JUDG.doc is visually handicapped.
Accordingly he has issued certificate to the Claimant.
The Certificate is at Exhibit-48.
The Cross- examination was declined by the Appellant-Insurance Company.
7. It is Claimant's case that, he was working as Cleaner and he was earning Rs.4,000/- per month.

8. While dealing with the issue of income of the Claimant, the Tribunal has observed that, the Claimant has not stated name of the employer and he was working as Cleaner, on that ground the Tribunal has held that, the amount of Rs.2,000/- to Rs.2,500/- monthly can be considered as income.
I am unable to understand the observations of the Tribunal as the Claimant was working as a cleaner.
He has lost vision of left eye.
He has specifically stated that, due to disability he has lost his job.
Considering these facts, I am considering Rs.4,000/- as monthly income of the Claimant.
The Tribunal has awarded lump-sump compensation, which is erroneous.
The Claimant has lost his left eye and he has suffered 20% disability to his leg.
The Tribunal should have given future prospects.
I am considering 40% future prospects as at the time of the accident the Claimant was 37 years N.S. Kamble page 5 of 8 90-FA-409-2008-JUDG.doc old.
The hospital bill shows that he has paid Rs.28,950/-.

Hence, I am considering this amount for hospital medical bills, and Rs.5,000/-
for eye treatment.
The Tribunal has not awarded attendance charges, I am considering it at Rs.25,000/-.
The Tribunal has not awarded amount for special diet, I am considering it at Rs.25,000/-.
The Tribunal has not awarded loss of comfort and amenities of life, I am considering it at Rs.40,000/-.
The Tribunal has not awarded conveyance charges, I am considering it at Rs.40,000/-.
The Tribunal has not awarded loss of earning during period of hospitalization, I am considering it at Rs.25,000/-.
9. Considering the above calculation's the Claimant is entitled for following compensation.
